prompt: Started by hand, `web` logged `connection refused` and exited. Why?
hint: What was Postgres doing at that moment?

choices.text: The password in `DATABASE_URL` did not match the one Postgres had
choices.why: A wrong password is refused by Postgres, not by the network.

choices.text: Postgres was still initialising and not listening yet
choices.why: Right: nothing made `web` wait for it.

choices.text: The two containers had been put on two different networks
choices.why: Both were on `shelfnet`, and `db` resolved to an address.

choices.text: Port 5432 was not published
choices.why: Containers on one network need no `-p` between them.

prompt: How did `shelf` reach Postgres with the host name `db`?
hint: What did the first command create?

choices.text: Docker added `db` to the host's `/etc/hosts`
choices.why: The host's files were not touched.

choices.text: `db` is a reserved name for databases
choices.why: Any container name would do.

choices.text: A network Ana created resolves names
choices.why: Right; lesson 23 shows how that works.

choices.text: Postgres announces itself on the network
choices.why: Postgres announces nothing; Docker answers the name.

prompt: Which problems of the by-hand setup does a Compose file solve? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: The start order depended on luck
choices.why: Yes: `depends_on` with a health condition fixes it.

choices.text: The setup lived in one person's shell history
choices.why: Yes: the file lives in the repository.

choices.text: Taking it down needed several commands
choices.why: Yes: `docker compose down`.

choices.text: Postgres needed more memory than the machine had
choices.why: Memory was never the problem.

prompt: For `web` to wait until `db` passes its health check, its `depends_on` sets `condition: service____`.
hint: The state `docker ps` shows in parentheses.

prompt: Why does the health check run `pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1` rather than plain `pg_isready`?
hint: What runs while the image initialises the database?

choices.text: `pg_isready` fails unless it is given a host to ask
choices.why: It works without one; it asks the local socket.

choices.text: Port 5432 is published only on 127.0.0.1
choices.why: It is not published at all.

choices.text: `-h` makes the check faster
choices.why: Speed is not the reason.

choices.text: The temporary setup server listens only on a socket
choices.why: Right: through TCP, only the real server can answer ready.

prompt: Put what `docker compose up -d` did in the order its output showed.
items: Create the network and the volume

prompt: Where did the prefix `shelf` in `shelf_default` and `shelf-db-1` come from?

choices.text: The directory the Compose file is in
choices.why: Right: the project name, which keeps two projects apart.

choices.text: The image name `shelf:1.5.0`
choices.why: `db` runs `postgres:17` and still got the prefix.

choices.text: A `name:` key at the top of `compose.yaml`
choices.why: Ana's file has none; the default is the directory.

choices.text: The first service in the file
choices.why: The first service is `db`.

prompt: `docker inspect` on `db` showed `POSTGRES_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/db_password` and no password. On `web` it showed the password. Why the difference?

choices.text: Compose encrypts secrets for `db` only
choices.why: Nothing is encrypted; the file is mounted as it is.

choices.text: Postgres reads a file, `shelf` a variable
choices.why: Right: a secret can only be a file for a program that reads one.

choices.text: `web` was started before the secret existed
choices.why: The secret existed before either container.

choices.text: The secret is only for images from Docker Hub
choices.why: Any image can mount it; the program has to read it.

prompt: Why did Ana add `*.env` and `db_password.txt` to `.dockerignore`?

choices.text: Compose refuses to start without them listed
choices.why: Compose does not read `.dockerignore`.

choices.text: To hide them from `docker compose ps`
choices.why: `ps` lists containers, not files.

choices.text: So no build copies them
choices.why: Right: the context is everything not ignored.

choices.text: Because the Dockerfile reads them
choices.why: It does not; they are for Compose.

prompt: After `docker compose down` and `up -d --wait`, the catalogue still had four books. Why?
hint: What did `docker volume ls` show after `down`?

choices.text: `down` only stops containers
choices.why: It removed them, and the network.

choices.text: Postgres keeps a copy in the image
choices.why: The image never changes.

choices.text: `shelf` re-inserted the fourth book
choices.why: `shelf` only seeds the three built-in books into an empty table.

choices.text: The named volume survived `down`
choices.why: Right: only `down -v` removes it.

prompt: After `up -d --build` with a new version of `shelf`, what happened to `db`?
hint: Read its line in the output.

choices.text: Nothing; its configuration had not changed
choices.why: Right: `Running`, left alone.

choices.text: It was rebuilt along with `web`
choices.why: `db` has no `build:`; it is an image from a registry.

choices.text: It was recreated, and its data lost
choices.why: Recreating keeps volumes anyway, and it was not recreated.

choices.text: It was restarted so that `web` could reconnect to it
choices.why: No restart was needed or shown.

prompt: What does `--wait` add to `docker compose up -d`?

choices.text: It waits for a key press before starting
choices.why: Nothing interactive happens.

choices.text: It returns once every checked service is healthy
choices.why: Right: what a script wants before its first request.

choices.text: It waits a fixed 30 seconds
choices.why: It waits for health, not for a clock.

choices.text: It retries services that fail
choices.why: Restarting is the restart policy's job.

prompt: Match each command to what it does.
hint: The table at the end of the section.

pairs.right: Removes containers and networks, keeps volumes
Runs a command inside a running service
Rebuilds images and recreates what changed

right_distractors: Moves a service to another machine

prompt: After the `INSERT`, how many books did `/books` return?
A colleague's Compose file has `depends_on: [db]` with no condition, and `web` sometimes fails at start. What is the fix?
hint: Started is not the same as ready.

choices.text: Add `sleep 10` before `shelf` starts
choices.why: A guess that fails on the slow day; and distroless has no shell for it.

choices.text: Publish `db`'s port
choices.why: Publishing changes nothing between containers on one network.

choices.text: Give `db` a health check and wait for `service_healthy`
choices.why: Right: `web` starts only when Postgres accepts connections.

choices.text: Remove `depends_on`
choices.why: Then the order is not even attempted.

prompt: At the end of a CI test run that used Compose, which command leaves nothing behind?

choices.text: `docker compose stop`
choices.why: Stopped containers, the network and the volume all remain.

choices.text: `docker compose down`
choices.why: The volume remains, with the test data.

choices.text: `docker compose down --rmi all`
choices.why: The images go too, and the volume still stays.

choices.text: `docker compose down -v`
choices.why: Right: containers, network and volumes.
